import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 712

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/712](https://www.erdosproblems.com/712)
- [Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved.
  Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
-/

namespace Erdos712

open Filter Asymptotics
open scoped Topology

/--
Determine, for any $k>r>2$, the limiting value as $n\to\infty$ of
$$\frac{\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)}{\binom{n}{r}},$$
where $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)$ is the largest number of $r$-edges which can placed on $n$ vertices
so that there exists no set of $k$ vertices which is covered by all $\binom{k}{r}$ possible
$r$-edges.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_712 :
    let L : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ := answer(sorry)
    ∀ k r : ℕ, 2 < r → r < k →
      Tendsto (fun n ↦ (Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n r k : ℝ) / n.choose r)
        atTop (𝓝 (L k r)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos712

reformulations.difference: Lean defines the density sequence for every natural n, including n < r where the binomial denominator is zero, rather than starting where the quotient has a positive denominator.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed r, the denominator is positive for all n ≥ r. The additional terms form a finite prefix and cannot change convergence or its limit. In scratch.lean, positive_denominator_tail_iff proves that the displayed Tendsto statement is equivalent to convergence of the sequence indexed by n + r.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/712 — statement, explanatory remarks, and current OPEN status; read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/712 with HTML output preserving the mathematics.
P. Erdős, On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved, Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25–42, §III.1; archival PDF: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf.
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliographic index identifying the cited 1981 paper.
review.notes: Checked the sole declaration and all relevant imported definitions. The extremal number is exactly the maximum size of an r-uniform clique-free edge family on n vertices. Lean checks established admissibility, attainment and maximality, and computed small examples. The answer is uniquely constrained on 2 < r < k, and any resulting limit lies in [0,1]. The website omits an explicit limit symbol in its displayed question, but calls the quantity 'this limit'; [Er81], §III.1 explicitly asks for a limit. All scratch checks compiled successfully without sorry-dependent proofs. The reviewed file is unchanged.
